reason: The text contains multiple regular human characters with dialogue, emotions, and opinions. The midwives Shiphrah and Puah are explicitly named and have direct lines of speech (verse 19: they respond to Pharaoh). They demonstrate clear emotions—specifically fear of God (verse 17: וַתִּירֶ֤אן הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים). They also express opinions through deliberate moral agency: they refuse to follow Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew male infants (verse 17) and provide reasoned justification for their disobedience (verse 19). Pharaoh himself also appears as a character with multiple lines of dialogue and intentions. This is fundamentally a narrative about ordinary people exercising moral judgment.
